title: A minimal CI workflow that calls the security gate
summary: A seed .github/workflows/ci.yml that runs on every pull request and push, no path filter: its first job calls security.yml, so every change is scanned; a `changes` job lets the project's costly jobs skip when only documentation changed. Guard CW-1..3 keeps that shape.

CI_WORKFLOW.prompt: Name of the CI workflow that must be green before a merge (its `name:`)

LIGHT_RUNNER.prompt: Runner label for the short jobs that need only bash, git, jq, the GitHub CLI and Node.js (ubuntu-latest keeps the 2-core runner; a self-hosted label works too)

postInstall: Skip this module if the project already has a CI workflow under another file name: two workflows with the same `name:` confuse whatever waits for it. Add the call to security.yml to yours instead (docs/conventions/security-workflow.md § Wiring).

Add the project's jobs (lint, tests, build) to .github/workflows/ci.yml, each with `needs: [security, changes]` and `if: needs.changes.outputs.code != 'false'`. With no code yet, leave the TODO(harness) block as it is: the gate alone is a valid CI.

Where a ruleset requires status checks, require the jobs of this workflow by their names (`Security / Enforcing (gitleaks + gate)` and yours): a job skipped because only documentation changed counts as passed.
This workflow has not run in your repository yet: open one pull request that only touches a Markdown file and check that the run starts, that `Security` runs and that your jobs are skipped.
